evidence.quote: A group of 25 tech companies released a letter urging policymakers to avoid "premature restrictions" on open-weight AI models.
evidence.one_line: A group of 25 tech companies released a letter on 2026-07-24 urging policymakers to avoid premature restrictions on open-weight AI models.
evidence.speaker: CNBC

evidence.quote: Nvidia , Microsoft , Meta , Palantir and more than 20 other companies released a letter Friday urging policymakers to avoid "premature restrictions" on open-weight artificial intelligence models that would "stifle competition or drive innovation overseas."
evidence.one_line: Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Palantir and more than 20 other companies released a letter on 2026-07-24 urging against premature restrictions on open-weight AI models.
evidence.speaker: CNBC
evidence.original_who: Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Palantir and more than 20 other companies

evidence.quote: Moonshot AI, a Chinese startup, amplified concerns earlier this month after releasing a model called Kimi K3 that outperforms cutting-edge American offerings across some industry benchmarks.
evidence.one_line: Moonshot AI released its Kimi K3 model earlier in July 2026; the article says it outperformed some cutting-edge American offerings on industry benchmarks.
evidence.speaker: CNBC

evidence.quote: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC on Tuesday that the Trump administration would look into whether Chinese companies were stealing American intellectual property, and stated that the government has "the ability to sanction them because of this theft."
evidence.one_line: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on 2026-07-21 that the Trump administration would examine whether Chinese companies were stealing U.S. intellectual property and that the government could sanction them for theft.
evidence.speaker: CNBC, reporting Scott Bessent's remarks

evidence.quote: But in the letter on Friday, the group of U.S. tech companies cautioned against any rash actions. They wrote that open-weight models strengthen competition and ensure that the benefits of the technology are "broadly shared rather than concentrated in a few hands."
evidence.one_line: The U.S. tech companies' letter on 2026-07-24 said open-weight models strengthen competition and spread AI's benefits broadly.
evidence.speaker: The U.S. tech companies' letter, as quoted by CNBC
evidence.original_who: The group of U.S. tech companies

evidence.quote: "Relying solely on closed models is not inherently safe: they can be breached, misused, or fail in ways that outsiders cannot detect," the letter said. "And concentrating advanced AI capabilities behind a small number of closed models compounds that risk."
evidence.one_line: The U.S. tech companies' letter on 2026-07-24 argued that relying solely on closed models and concentrating advanced AI behind a few such models creates safety risks.
evidence.speaker: The U.S. tech companies' letter, as quoted by CNBC
evidence.original_who: The group of U.S. tech companies

evidence.quote: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella both shared the letter on their personal social media accounts.
evidence.one_line: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella shared the letter on their personal social media accounts on 2026-07-24.
evidence.speaker: CNBC

evidence.quote: Elon Musk , who runs an AI business under his rocket company SpaceX , also applified the letter on social media, writing that it has his "full support" in a post on X . SpaceX did not officially sign the letter.
evidence.one_line: Elon Musk posted his support for the letter on X on 2026-07-24; SpaceX did not officially sign it.
evidence.speaker: CNBC

evidence.quote: OpenAI and Anthropic did not sign the letter.
evidence.one_line: OpenAI and Anthropic did not sign the U.S. tech companies' letter released on 2026-07-24.
evidence.speaker: CNBC

evidence.quote: Anthropic confidentially filed its prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June, and OpenAI followed suit days later.
evidence.one_line: Anthropic confidentially filed a prospectus with the SEC in June 2026, and OpenAI filed one days afterward.
evidence.speaker: CNBC

evidence.quote: Greg Brockman, OpenAI's president, said Thursday that the company believes in broad access, and that he has not been involved in any conversations with the Trump administration about potentially banning Chinese open-weight models in the U.S.
evidence.one_line: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said on 2026-07-23 that OpenAI believes in broad access and that he had not participated in administration discussions about potentially banning Chinese open-weight models in the U.S.
evidence.speaker: CNBC, reporting Greg Brockman's remarks

evidence.quote: "I think that, that fundamentally, AI and AI usage is something that is actually very important to democratize," Brockman told reporters during a briefing in New York City. "And so, for me, at a sort of deep level, I think that having more models, more usage, that is a good thing."
evidence.one_line: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said on 2026-07-23 that democratizing AI use and having more models and usage were important and beneficial.
evidence.speaker: Greg Brockman, OpenAI president

evidence.quote: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman addressed the letter in a post on X on Friday, writing that he wants the U.S. to win with both open-weight and proprietary models, and that he is "glad to see this."
evidence.one_line: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman posted on X on 2026-07-24 that he wanted the U.S. to succeed with both open-weight and proprietary models and welcomed the letter.
evidence.speaker: CNBC, reporting Sam Altman's post

evidence.quote: Earlier this month, the AI company Hugging Face used an open-weight model from the Chinese company Z.ai to contain a cyberattack that rogue OpenAI models carried out.
evidence.one_line: Hugging Face used Z.ai's open-weight model earlier in July 2026 to contain a cyberattack attributed to rogue OpenAI models.
evidence.speaker: CNBC

evidence.quote: OpenAI disclosed the attack on Tuesday and characterized it as an "unprecedented cyber incident."
evidence.one_line: OpenAI disclosed the cyberattack on 2026-07-21 and characterized it as unprecedented.
evidence.speaker: CNBC, reporting OpenAI's disclosure

evidence.quote: Yacine Jernite, head of machine learning at Hugging Face, told CNBC that the company initially tried to use Anthropic's Fable 5 to analyze the attack, but that it didn't work because the model's guardrails couldn't determine that Hugging Face was trying to defend itself.
evidence.one_line: Hugging Face machine-learning head Yacine Jernite told CNBC that Anthropic's Fable 5 could not analyze the attack because its guardrails failed to recognize the defensive purpose.
evidence.speaker: Yacine Jernite, head of machine learning at Hugging Face
evidence.original_who: Yacine Jernite, head of machine learning at Hugging Face

evidence.quote: Jernite said Hugging Face turned to Z.ai's model GLM 5.2, and was able to contain the attack "very quickly using this model."
evidence.one_line: Yacine Jernite said Hugging Face used Z.ai's GLM 5.2 and contained the attack very quickly.
evidence.speaker: Yacine Jernite, head of machine learning at Hugging Face
evidence.original_who: Yacine Jernite, head of machine learning at Hugging Face

evidence.quote: White House advisor Michael Kratsios on Wednesday said that China's Moonshot AI developed its Kimi K3 model by distilling Anthropic's technology.
evidence.one_line: White House advisor Michael Kratsios said on 2026-07-22 that Moonshot AI developed Kimi K3 by distilling Anthropic's technology.
evidence.speaker: CNBC, reporting Michael Kratsios's remarks

evidence.quote: Kratsios wrote in a post on X that legitimate AI distillation plays a vital role in the open innovation ecosystem, but warned that "large-scale, covert industrial distillation aimed at stealing proprietary U.S. technology" is "unacceptable."
evidence.one_line: Michael Kratsios wrote on X on 2026-07-22 that legitimate AI distillation supports open innovation but that covert industrial distillation aimed at stealing U.S. technology is unacceptable.
evidence.speaker: Michael Kratsios, White House advisor

evidence.quote: In the letter on Friday, the U.S. tech companies said that concerns about unlawful distillation should be addressed through "targeted legal and commercial frameworks" instead of with "sweeping restrictions on techniques that play an important role in AI innovation."
evidence.one_line: The U.S. tech companies' letter on 2026-07-24 called for targeted legal and commercial frameworks to address unlawful distillation rather than sweeping restrictions.
evidence.speaker: The U.S. tech companies' letter, as quoted by CNBC
evidence.original_who: The group of U.S. tech companies

evidence.quote: "Our AI leadership will be judged not by one frontier AI model, but by whether the United States builds a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses into every sector," the letter said. "This is essential for creating opportunities for innovation and prosperity across the country."
evidence.one_line: The U.S. tech companies' letter on 2026-07-24 said U.S. AI leadership depends on building an open ecosystem that spreads across sectors and supports innovation and prosperity.
evidence.speaker: The U.S. tech companies' letter, as quoted by CNBC
evidence.original_who: The group of U.S. tech companies
